# Existing empty destinations require explicit opt-in, for both CAR versions.
cp empty empty-v1.car
! car create --version=1 --file=empty-v1.car foo.txt
stderr 'output file already exists'
cmp empty empty-v1.car
car create --append --version=1 --file=empty-v1.car foo.txt
car verify empty-v1.car

cp empty empty-v2.car
! car create --version=2 --file=empty-v2.car foo.txt
stderr 'output file already exists'
cmp empty empty-v2.car
car create --append --version=2 --file=empty-v2.car foo.txt
car verify empty-v2.car

# Existing populated CARs are rejected without changing their contents.
cp empty-v1.car original-v1.car
! car create --version=1 --file=empty-v1.car bar.txt
stderr 'output file already exists'
cmp empty-v1.car original-v1.car

cp empty-v2.car original-v2.car
! car create --version=2 --file=empty-v2.car bar.txt
stderr 'output file already exists'
cmp empty-v2.car original-v2.car

# --append retains the existing header checks for finalized CARs.
! car create --append --version=1 --file=empty-v1.car bar.txt
stderr 'cannot resume on file with mismatching data header'
cmp empty-v1.car original-v1.car
! car create --append --version=2 --file=empty-v2.car bar.txt
stderr 'cannot resume on file with mismatching data header'
cmp empty-v2.car original-v2.car

# A failed create leaves an unfinished CAR that --append can resume.
! car create --version=1 --file=resume-v1.car missing.txt
exists resume-v1.car
car create --append --version=1 --file=resume-v1.car foo.txt
car verify resume-v1.car
! car create --version=2 --file=resume-v2.car missing.txt
exists resume-v2.car
car create --append --version=2 --file=resume-v2.car foo.txt
car verify resume-v2.car

# Arbitrary data is never truncated, even with --append.
cp foo.txt random.car
! car create --file=random.car bar.txt
stderr 'output file already exists'
cmp random.car foo.txt
! car create --append --file=random.car bar.txt
cmp random.car foo.txt

# A directory or symlink is also an existing destination.
mkdir directory.car
! car create --file=directory.car foo.txt
stderr 'output file already exists'
[symlink] symlink linked.car -> original-v2.car
[symlink] ! car create --file=linked.car bar.txt
[symlink] stderr 'output file already exists'
[symlink] cmp original-v2.car empty-v2.car
[symlink] symlink dangling.car -> absent.car
[symlink] ! car create --file=dangling.car foo.txt
[symlink] stderr 'output file already exists'
[symlink] ! exists absent.car

# --append can also create a new destination.
car create --append --version=1 --file=new-v1.car foo.txt
car verify new-v1.car
car create --append --version=2 --file=new-v2.car foo.txt
car verify new-v2.car

-- empty --
-- foo.txt --
foo content
-- bar.txt --
bar content
